discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

motivation: For 25 years gamma-ray bursts were one of astrophysics' deepest mysteries, with their distance scale unknown. In 1997 Costa and Frontera, leading the BeppoSAX Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor and Wide Field Camera effort, discovered the fading X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228. This gave the arcminute positions that made rapid optical and radio follow-up possible. Kulkarni and collaborators then measured the redshift of GRB 970508 and detected its radio afterglow. Together these results showed that gamma-ray bursts lie at cosmological distances and are the most luminous explosions known, with relativistic outflows. The work opened the modern era of time-domain, multi-wavelength astrophysics. It led to the link between long bursts and the deaths of massive stars, to probes of the earliest galaxies and reionization, and to the rapid-response strategies that made the multi-messenger identification of the neutron-star merger GW170817 possible.
